about: Japanese text cut into the phrases a line may break between, as BudouX 0.10's Japanese model finds them in JavaScript: the site marks them with <wbr> (packages/jsx phrasesOf), the iOS app keeps each whole (PochicalDesign Phrases.split). BudouX scores the text in UTF-16 code units, so an emoji outside the BMP counts as two, and never cuts between the halves of a surrogate pair. Text with no Hiragana, Katakana or Han, by Unicode script extensions (which take in 、。ー and the half-width kana, but not full-width Latin letters or ！？), stays whole, though BudouX would cut it. Every other `expected` is what BudouX's own parser gives for `text`.
